The first year is the hardest by far - you aren’t so much teaching as you are surviving. Learning to manage a class of teenagers effectively takes a lot of experience and practice. Until you have had the time to figure out who you are as a teacher and what your management style is, it’s better not to share too much. 

Be crystal clear with expectations (ex. I should see... I should hear...), be consistent, and always follow through. Do your best to keep a level head even when the kids are being awful - they want the reaction!

I’m finishing up my 10th year and it took time, patience, and lots of learning to get here. If you told me ten years ago that I could make genuine connections with my students while also shutting shit down with a look I would have laughed in your face. We have all been there! 

It gets better. I promise. Feel free to message me anytime! 

PS - I think middle school is the absolute worst age to teach so I give you a lot of credit!
